text: Gentlemen. Ladies. Men of capital. Sit down, don't touch anything, and look at this.
I'm the founder of En-detz Labs, and this is Union Clef. The lab boys tell me it's the future. I tell the lab boys what the future is. Today, for once, we agree.

Here's the situation. Your artificial intelligence can write a sonnet, pass the bar exam, and explain your own divorce to you. Put it in Minecraft, and it cannot punch a tree. Embarrassing. For everybody.

So we built it a body. Your agent plugs in over M C P, or Python if you're the old-fashioned type, and gets sixty levers. Look around. Go there. Mine that. Hit him. Build this. Your agent does the thinking, we do the arms and legs. That's called division of labor, boys. Look it up.

Now, walking. Any fool can walk. Our pathfinder, Tungsten, doesn't guess where a player can go. It runs a physics simulation of the player's body, and plans the route on that. Parkour jumps. Bridges over nothing. Pillars. Swimming. A one-block lane between two rivers of lava.
The lab boys built eighteen obstacle courses. It passes eighteen out of eighteen. I asked for nineteen. They said there are only eighteen. So build more courses!

Skeletons. They shoot arrows, and arrows hurt. So every single tick the bot simulates eighteen different ways to step, and takes the one the arrow misses. Ten arrows. Before: twenty-four points of damage. Now: zero. The skeleton has filed a complaint. Denied.

And it lives off the land. Empty pockets, brand new world. Wood, stone, iron tools in about eight minutes. At night it digs a hole, puts a lid on it, and waits for the morning. Frankly, that's my retirement plan.

Now here's my favorite. The nether portal. Normally you need a diamond pickaxe. We don't have one. Budget cuts. So the bot pours lava into a mould, pours water on top, casts ten blocks of obsidian by hand, lights it, and walks straight into hell.
This morning, that worked one time in eight. By dinner, five times in nine. That's four times better. I had the lab boys check the math. They're still checking.
Now, the numbers. Investors love numbers. For four months this lab produced almost nothing. Then in July we put an A I agent on the job of building the A I. Look at that line.
Three thousand seven hundred commits. A hundred and thirty-one releases. Nobody in this building has slept since July. Nobody needs to. The machine doesn't sleep, and neither does my accountant.
What's next? We beat the game. The End. The dragon. We are not there yet. The dragon remains, for the moment, completely unbothered. Give us your money, and we will bother it.

Remember the name. En-detz Labs. It's open source, so technically nobody can own it. Invest anyway. We'll figure out the details later. The lab boys are telling me to stop talking now. I'm not going to.
